at_the_boundary_species.direction: abSENSE OVER-predicts what a Salix homolog would have scored. An expected score that is too high makes an observed absence look more surprising than it is, which under-estimates detection_failure_prob and over-calls surprising_absence.
at_the_boundary_species.species: Salix purpurea -- the rank-18 boundary. Every HDF flag on this pool is a prediction at this species.

absense_calibration.headline: abSENSE flags are worst calibrated at exactly the boundary that defines this pool, and biased in the direction that over-calls a young gene. Quote the flag with this number, never alone.
absense_calibration.measured: 2026-09-09, abSENSE --predall over 868,127 predicted-vs-observed bitscore pairs (ms2-lsg analyses/absense_hdf, jobs 48015768_1/_2)
absense_calibration.this_is_the_optimistic_bound: It is measured in-sample, and on the wrong genes: a Salix pair only exists for a gene that HAS a Salix homolog, which by definition is not an LSG. For a real PS18 gene the Salix prediction is pure out-of-sample extrapolation. 0.59-0.61 is what the model achieves at that boundary on the easy cases.

note: abSENSE calibration measured for the LSG QC layer. Until 2026-10-14 it lived only in the committed data/meta/manifest.json (lsg_qc.absense_calibration), so a full rebuild, which rewrites the manifest first, could not pass patch_lsg_qc.py. Extracted verbatim from origin/main data 0.18.1.
